cards.definition: **Definition.** A path anchored according to the active platform's filesystem rules while still not proving target existence accessibility identity stability or safe authorization.
major_error_concepts: Treating absolute spelling as proof of a present readable stable file.
cards.prompt: Define Python absolute path. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An absolute path is anchored according to the active platform's filesystem rules.
Absolute-path status does not prove that the target exists.
Absolute-path status does not prove that the process can access the target.
Absolute-path status does not establish stable target identity across filesystem changes.
Absolute-path status does not authorize an otherwise disallowed operation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A change performed through one reference path that becomes observable through every other path reaching the same mutable object while unrelated equal objects remain unchanged.
major_error_concepts: Updating only the syntactic target name in the reference graph after mutation.
cards.prompt: Define Python alias-visible mutation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Alias-visible mutation changes a mutable object through one reference path.
Every other reference path reaching that same object can observe the changed state.
An unrelated object remains unchanged even when it compares equal to the mutated object.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Iterator consumption and truth testing that returns `False` after the first falsey item or `True` after ordinary exhaustion including the vacuous true empty-input case.
major_error_concepts: Requiring one truthy item for all or evaluating later items after a falsey result.
cards.prompt: Define Python `all` short circuit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Python `all` consumes and truth-tests encountered items in traversal order.
The first falsey item causes `all` to return `False`.
Items after the first falsey item are not consumed by that call.
Ordinary exhaustion without a falsey item causes `all` to return `True`.
An empty iterable therefore produces vacuous `True`.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Left-to-right operand evaluation that returns the first falsey operand or the final operand and skips every later operand once the result is determined.
major_error_concepts: Claiming `and` always returns a Boolean or evaluates both operands eagerly.
cards.prompt: Define Python `and` short circuit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Left-to-right operand evaluation that returns the first falsey operand or the final operand and skips every later operand once the result is determined.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Iterator consumption and truth testing that returns `True` after the first truthy item or `False` after ordinary exhaustion while skipping later items after success.
major_error_concepts: Materializing and evaluating every item before deciding the any result.
cards.prompt: Define Python `any` short circuit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Python `any` consumes and truth-tests encountered items in traversal order.
The first truthy item causes `any` to return `True`.
Items after the first truthy item are not consumed by that call.
Ordinary exhaustion without a truthy item causes `any` to return `False`.
An empty iterable therefore produces `False`.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The complete record from each evaluated supplied value or default to its callee parameter binding including collection order and any rejected unmatched or duplicate inputs.
major_error_concepts: Inferring local parameter values after body effects have already changed referenced objects.
cards.prompt: Define Python argument-binding map. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An argument-binding map records every evaluated supplied value and its callee parameter destination.
The map records every default value used for an unsupplied parameter.
The map preserves collection order for variadic parameters.
The map records unmatched inputs rejected by binding.
The map records duplicate inputs rejected for one parameter.

accepted_variants: The callable and arguments are evaluated before its body; a failure prevents the body and does not undo earlier effects. In f(b=mark('keyword',1), *mark('star',[])), star is evaluated before keyword.
cards.definition: Call evaluation evaluates the callable and arguments before the callee body begins. Ordinary positional arguments are evaluated left to right, but a legal mixture of explicit keywords and * unpacking must follow the call rules: positional/* arguments are processed before keyword/** arguments even when a * argument is written later. An evaluation or unpacking failure stops the call; earlier side effects remain.
major_error_concepts: Assuming textual keyword position places its evaluation before a later starred positional argument.
Running the callee body before argument evaluation/binding succeeds.
cards.prompt: How are Python call arguments evaluated before the body runs? Include the special case of * unpacking written after an explicit keyword.
required_concepts: Argument evaluation precedes callee-body execution, with earlier side effects retained if evaluation fails.
A starred positional argument can be evaluated before a keyword expression that appears earlier in the source; do not apply a blanket textual-order rule to that mixture.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** The rule that assertion execution can be removed by optimization settings making assertions unsuitable for mandatory validation authorization cleanup or any required state transition.

**Worked check.** Run `assert ready` normally and with `python -O`: only the normal run checks it, so the assertion cannot enforce an input or security contract.
major_error_concepts: Relying on assertion evaluation to sanitize input or create required state.
cards.prompt: What boundary or limitation does Python assertion-enablement boundary impose?
required_concepts: Python optimization settings can remove assertion execution.
A mandatory validation decision must remain active when assertions are removed.
Authorization decisions must not depend on an assertion side effect or result.
Required cleanup must not depend on assertion execution.
Any required state transition must occur outside the removable assertion boundary.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** A debug-oriented statement that raises `AssertionError` when an internal predicate is false under ordinary enabled execution and whose expression should not carry required program effects.

**Worked check.** `assert n > 0, 'n'` continues for `n=2` and raises `AssertionError('n')` for `n=0` when assertions are enabled.
major_error_concepts: Using assertion as the only check on untrusted input or required side effects.
cards.prompt: What does Python assertion statement diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A Python assertion is a debug-oriented check of an internal predicate.
Under ordinary enabled execution, a false assertion predicate raises `AssertionError`.
An assertion expression should not perform effects required for correct program behavior.
Assertion execution may be removed by supported optimization settings.
Assertions are unsuitable for mandatory external-input validation.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** The separation between optional internal invariant diagnostics and mandatory boundary validation whose failure interface must remain active in every supported execution configuration.

**Worked check.** `assert token` can disappear under `-O`; `if not token: raise ValueError('token')` remains, so persistent input validation uses the explicit branch.
major_error_concepts: Calling an enabled assertion equivalent to a durable input-validation contract.
cards.prompt: What boundary or limitation does Python assertion-validation distinction impose?
required_concepts: An assertion expresses an optional internal-invariant diagnostic.
Boundary validation enforces a mandatory acceptance rule for untrusted or external state.
Assertion failure conventionally signals a programming-invariant defect.
Validation failure uses the documented interface appropriate to the caller or input contract.
Validation remains active across every supported execution configuration.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** The ordered runtime transition that evaluates the right-hand expression and then applies the resulting object to each assignment target according to that target's semantics.

**Worked check.** With `x=1`, `x=x+1` reads the old binding on the right, computes `2`, then rebinds `x`; it does not mutate the integer object `1`.
major_error_concepts: Updating a target before all required right-hand values have been evaluated.
cards.prompt: Given x = 1, trace x = x + 1. In what order do the right-hand lookup, addition, and target binding occur, and is the integer object 1 mutated?
required_concepts: A Python assignment event first evaluates the right-hand expression.
Right-hand evaluation produces the object supplied to the assignment targets.
The event then applies that object to each target in the language-defined order.
Each target is processed according to its target-specific semantics.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The name attribute subscription slice or unpacking pattern designated to receive or mutate the result of an assignment operation under its target-specific semantics.
major_error_concepts: Assuming all assignment syntax creates or rebinds a local name.
cards.prompt: Define Python assignment target. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A Python assignment target designates where an assignment result is applied.
A target may be a name or an attribute reference.
A target may be a subscription or slice.
A target may be an unpacking pattern.
Each target form applies assignment under its own binding or mutation semantics.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A read-operation-write target form such as `+=` whose exact behavior may update an object in place or produce a replacement before target assignment depending on operand protocols.
major_error_concepts: Expanding augmented assignment to ordinary assignment without checking single target evaluation and in-place behavior.
cards.prompt: Define Python augmented assignment. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Python augmented assignment is a target read-operation-write form such as `+=`.
The operation may update the existing object in place.
The operation may instead produce a replacement object before assignment back to the target.
Operand protocols determine which behavior occurs for the selected types.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Use of `raise` without an expression inside an active handler to propagate the currently handled exception while retaining its original traceback more directly than replacement construction.
major_error_concepts: Using bare raise outside an active exception context or calling it new construction.
cards.prompt: Define Python bare re-raise. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A bare `raise` inside an active exception handler propagates the currently handled exception.
The bare form reuses the active exception object rather than constructing a replacement.
The bare form preserves the original traceback relation more directly than raising a newly constructed exception.
A bare `raise` without an active handled exception is invalid.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A paired failing and repaired execution using matched source lineage input environment and observations so the target symptom and relevant state transition can be compared directly.
major_error_concepts: Using unmatched fixtures and calling their output difference repair evidence.
cards.prompt: Define Python before-after reproducer. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A before-after reproducer contains paired failing and repaired executions.
The pair uses matched source lineage with only the declared repair edit differing.
The pair uses matched input, initial state, and environment.
The pair uses matched observation boundaries and procedures.
The target symptom is compared directly across the pair.
The relevant causal state transition is also compared across the pair.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A file-object mode that reads and writes bytes-like values without automatic text encoding decoding or newline translation by the text layer.
major_error_concepts: Passing a string directly to a binary write and assuming implicit encoding.
cards.prompt: Define Python binary file mode. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A file-object mode that reads and writes bytes-like values without automatic text encoding decoding or newline translation by the text layer.

accepted_variants: It returns True or False if truth testing succeeds. A custom __bool__ can increment an attribute before returning True, or can raise; bool(x) does not automatically replace x with a Boolean.
cards.definition: bool(x) applies Python truth-value testing and, when it succeeds, returns True or False. It does not inherently retype x, but the truth protocol can call user code, so bool(x) is not a universal no-mutation/no-exception guarantee.
major_error_concepts: Claiming bool is universally free of mutation, exceptions or user-code execution.
Claiming bool necessarily changes the input object's type.
cards.prompt: What does bool(x) return, and can evaluating it execute user code or have side effects?
required_concepts: Successful bool(x) returns a Boolean according to truth-value testing.
Truth hooks may run user code, mutate state or raise; conversion does not itself mean x is rebound or retyped.

cards.definition: **Definition.** One of the two objects `True` and `False` used as canonical truth results while remaining distinct from the broader truth-value testing of arbitrary objects.
major_error_concepts: Calling every falsey object the Boolean object `False` and discarding its original type.
cards.prompt: Define Python Boolean value. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: One of the two objects `True` and `False` used as canonical truth results while remaining distinct from the broader truth-value testing of arbitrary objects.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A retry contract with explicit eligible failures maximum attempts stop condition delay policy and final disposition preventing unbounded loops and misleading success-only evidence.
major_error_concepts: Catching and retrying forever without an attempt cap or failure receipt.
cards.prompt: Define Python bounded retry policy. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A bounded retry policy declares which failure classes are retryable.
The policy declares a maximum number of attempts.
The policy declares an earlier stop condition when further attempts are not justified.
The policy declares any delay or backoff behavior.
The policy declares the final disposition after attempts are exhausted.
The policy retains failed-attempt evidence rather than reporting only eventual success.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A declared division of relevant input states by the first-match outcomes of one conditional including overlaps unreachable regions and any uncovered fallback region.
major_error_concepts: Listing branch labels without specifying which inputs reach each one under clause order.
cards.prompt: Define Python branch partition. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A Python branch partition divides the relevant input states for one conditional.
Each state is classified by the first matching branch outcome.
The partition records overlapping branch conditions.
The partition records unreachable regions.
The partition records any input region handled only by a fallback or left uncovered.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The iteration state condition evidence and exact `break` site responsible for an interrupted loop exit kept distinct from ordinary exhaustion and exception termination.
major_error_concepts: Reporting early exit without evidence of which condition and item authorized it.
cards.prompt: Define Python break provenance. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Python break provenance identifies the exact `break` site that interrupted a loop.
The record captures the iteration state at that site.
The record captures the condition and evidence that caused the `break` to execute.
A break exit is distinct from ordinary iterator or condition exhaustion.
A break exit is distinct from exception termination.

accepted_variants: break targets the nearest loop and skips that loop's else if the break completes. A surrounding finally still runs first and can replace the pending transfer.
cards.definition: break requests departure from the nearest enclosing loop and, if that transfer completes, skips its loop-else suite. Applicable finally and context-manager cleanup runs before departure. Cleanup that raises or otherwise replaces the pending transfer can change the eventual outcome.
major_error_concepts: Skipping required cleanup or treating break as exit from every enclosing loop.
cards.prompt: Describe Python break, including its target, loop-else behavior, and cleanup before departure.
required_concepts: The intended target is the nearest enclosing loop; a completed break skips its else suite.
Applicable cleanup runs before departure and may replace the pending transfer.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Evidence that the recorded execution actually reaches and satisfies any condition for a configured breakpoint before termination rather than inferring reachability from source placement.
major_error_concepts: Concluding a branch never runs because a misconfigured breakpoint did not pause.
cards.prompt: Define Python breakpoint reachability. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Breakpoint reachability requires evidence that the recorded execution reaches the configured source or function boundary.
A conditional breakpoint also requires evidence that its pause condition is satisfied.
The reachability claim is scoped to the bound source, input, environment, and control path.
Source placement alone does not establish dynamic reachability.
Termination before the breakpoint is recorded as nonreach evidence rather than a silent absence.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A configured source or function location at which debugger-controlled execution requests a pause before or after a documented boundary so state can be inspected.
major_error_concepts: Treating a configured but unreached breakpoint as evidence about runtime state.
cards.prompt: Define Python debugger breakpoint. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A debugger breakpoint is configured at a specified source or function location.
The breakpoint requests a pause when debugger-controlled execution reaches its trigger boundary.
The breakpoint contract declares whether the pause is before or after the associated operation.
Configuring a breakpoint does not prove that the recorded execution reaches it.
A pause may be superseded by debugger conditions or other stop behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A handler whose accepted hierarchy covers many unrelated failures and can therefore hide programming defects cancellation signals or invalid state unless its boundary and disposition are explicit.
major_error_concepts: Calling a broad catch robust because the program continues after every failure.
cards.prompt: Define Python broad exception catch. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A broad exception catch accepts a hierarchy covering many unrelated failures.
The protected-region boundary of a broad exception catch determines which operations can be intercepted.
A broad catch can conceal programming defects behind an expected-failure disposition.
A broad catch can intercept cancellation or control-related signals depending on the hierarchy selected.
Safe use requires an explicit evidence and propagation disposition for unmatched meanings.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A mutable sequence of byte integers supporting in-place binary edits while remaining distinct from immutable bytes and Unicode string values.
major_error_concepts: Treating bytearray mutation as text-character replacement under an implicit encoding.
cards.prompt: Define Python bytearray object. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A mutable sequence of byte integers supporting in-place binary edits while remaining distinct from immutable bytes and Unicode string values.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Conversion of bytes to a Unicode string using a named codec and error policy whose correctness depends on the byte sequence matching the intended encoding.
major_error_concepts: Selecting a codec from successful output appearance alone or calling bytes already textual.
cards.prompt: Define Python bytes decoding. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Conversion of bytes to a Unicode string using a named codec and error policy whose correctness depends on the byte sequence matching the intended encoding.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An immutable sequence of integer byte values from zero through 255 used for encoded or binary data independently of Unicode text meaning.
major_error_concepts: Treating bytes as a string with interchangeable indexing and concatenation operands.
cards.prompt: Define Python bytes object. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An immutable sequence of integer byte values from zero through 255 used for encoded or binary data independently of Unicode text meaning.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A value supplied by one call after its argument expression is evaluated and before it is matched to a compatible parameter or variadic collection.
major_error_concepts: Calling a parameter's default value an argument supplied explicitly by every caller.
cards.prompt: Define Python call argument. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A value supplied by one call after its argument expression is evaluated and before it is matched to a compatible parameter or variadic collection.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The count and accepted arrangement of supplied argument values relative to required optional and variadic parameters rather than a single universal number for every function.
major_error_concepts: Counting keyword labels as separate values or ignoring variadic acceptance rules.
cards.prompt: Define Python call arity. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Python call arity describes the count and accepted arrangement of supplied argument values.
Arity is evaluated relative to required parameters.
Optional parameters affect the accepted range of supplied values.
Variadic parameters can make the accepted arity open-ended.
A Python function need not have one universal accepted argument count for every call form.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An expression that evaluates the callable and argument expressions performs argument binding invokes the resulting callable and yields its return value or propagated exception.
major_error_concepts: Jumping from written arguments to body execution without evaluating the callable or binding parameters.
cards.prompt: Define Python call expression. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A Python call expression evaluates the expression that supplies the callable.
The call expression evaluates its argument expressions.
The call performs argument binding against the resulting callable.
The bound callable is invoked.
The call expression yields the callable's return value or a propagated exception.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The ordered active-frame nesting produced by calls whose top frame currently executes and whose lower frames preserve pending continuation or exception propagation sites.
major_error_concepts: Treating traceback print order or source order as identical to active-frame nesting automatically.
cards.prompt: Define Python call stack. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A Python call stack is the ordered nesting of active execution frames produced by calls.
The top frame is the frame currently executing.
Each lower active frame preserves a pending continuation site.
Lower frames also preserve sites through which exceptions may propagate.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A completed-execution structure whose nodes are call instances and whose edges identify caller-to-callee invocations while preserving order repeated calls and returned outcomes.
major_error_concepts: Collapsing repeated call instances into one function-definition node and losing execution multiplicity.
cards.prompt: Define Python call tree. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A Python call tree represents one completed execution.
Each tree node is one call instance rather than merely one function name.
Each edge records a caller-to-callee invocation.
The tree preserves sibling call order and repeated calls.
The tree records the returned outcome of each call instance.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The first call phase that resolves and evaluates the expression before parentheses to an object whose call protocol may accept or reject the supplied arguments.
major_error_concepts: Assuming the textual identifier always names the originally defined function at call time.
cards.prompt: Define Python callable evaluation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The first call phase that resolves and evaluates the expression before parentheses to an object whose call protocol may accept or reject the supplied arguments.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The new execution frame created for an accepted function call containing parameter bindings local state code position and return relationship to the caller.
major_error_concepts: Updating caller locals directly merely because parameter names match caller names.
cards.prompt: Define Python callee frame. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The new execution frame created for an accepted function call containing parameter bindings local state code position and return relationship to the caller.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The suspended or continuing execution context that initiated a call and will receive the returned value or propagated exception at the call-expression position.
major_error_concepts: Replacing the caller frame with the callee frame during a nested call trace.
cards.prompt: Define Python caller frame. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The suspended or continuing execution context that initiated a call and will receive the returned value or propagated exception at the call-expression position.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The joined first-violating transition hypothesis-loop and breakpoint evidence that links one proposed defect to the target symptom while recording still-viable alternative explanations.
major_error_concepts: Calling source proximity or a single matching value proof of causation.
cards.prompt: Define Python causal-defect evidence. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Causal-defect evidence includes the first observed invariant-violating transition.
The evidence includes a falsifiable causal hypothesis linking that transition to the target symptom.
The evidence includes controlled-probe or breakpoint observations that support the predicted link.
The evidence includes a matched intervention or repair result when available.
Still-viable alternative explanations are recorded rather than omitted.
The conclusion is bounded to the target reproducer and tested conditions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The incorrect source rule assumption input-state transition or interface decision whose controlled correction explains removal of the target failure under the specified conditions.
major_error_concepts: Defining causal defect as whichever line the debugger currently highlights.
cards.prompt: Define Python causal defect. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A causal defect is an incorrect source rule, assumption, input-state transition, or interface decision.
The defect is linked to the target failure under specified execution conditions.
A controlled correction of the defect removes the target causal path.
The correction preserves declared unaffected behavior in the evaluated scope.
A correlated source location without controlled correction is not yet causal-defect evidence.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** A falsifiable statement linking a proposed earlier source or state condition to the target symptom through a predicted observable execution difference under a controlled probe.

**Worked check.** Hypothesis: trimming input caused the missing leading space. Prediction: disabling only `.strip()` restores that space on the same fixture.
major_error_concepts: Writing a vague guess with no observable prediction or disconfirming outcome.
cards.prompt: What does Python causal hypothesis diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A causal hypothesis proposes an earlier source or state condition that produces the target symptom.
The hypothesis specifies a mechanism connecting that condition to the symptom.
The hypothesis predicts an observable execution difference under a controlled probe.
The prediction is declared before the probe result is inspected.
An incompatible valid probe result can falsify or narrow the hypothesis.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A comparison sequence such as `a < b < c` that evaluates the middle expression once and requires each adjacent comparison to succeed with short-circuit behavior.
major_error_concepts: Rewriting a chain in a way that evaluates a stateful middle expression twice.
cards.prompt: Define Python chained comparison. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A chained comparison evaluates a sequence of adjacent comparisons such as `a < b < c`.
The shared middle expression is evaluated only once.
Every adjacent comparison reached in the chain must succeed for the chain to succeed.
A failing adjacent comparison short-circuits the remaining chain.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** The separation between releasing resources or preserving evidence and restoring the program's declared invariant so cleanup completion alone never licenses a successful recovery claim.

**Worked check.** A `finally` block can close a file after a failed upload, but closing it does not retract bytes already accepted by the remote service; recovery needs a separate action.
major_error_concepts: Calling resource release business-state repair or treating continued execution as invariant restoration.
cards.prompt: What boundary or limitation does Python cleanup-recovery distinction impose?
required_concepts: Cleanup releases resources or preserves failure evidence after a disrupted operation.
Recovery restores the declared program invariant needed for safe downstream execution.
Successful cleanup does not by itself establish successful recovery.
A recovery claim requires explicit post-handler invariant evidence.
The disposition may clean up and still propagate or terminate rather than continue.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The value error or operation-specific rejection produced when code attempts ordinary I/O through a file object after its closed state is established.
major_error_concepts: Assuming a file name keeps the prior file object usable after closure.
cards.prompt: Define Python closed-file operation failure. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The value error or operation-specific rejection produced when code attempts ordinary I/O through a file object after its closed state is established.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A nested function's retained lexical association to an enclosing variable location used by later calls rather than an automatic frozen copy of the value at definition.
major_error_concepts: Treating every closure as copying all enclosing values into immutable constants.
cards.prompt: Define Python closure read binding. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A closure read binding retains a lexical association from a nested function to an enclosing variable location.
Later calls use that retained association to read the enclosing binding.
The closure does not automatically freeze a copy of the enclosing value at function-definition time.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The value produced by an equality ordering identity or membership comparison and then truth-tested when used by control flow rather than assumed to be the compared operands.
major_error_concepts: Jumping directly from operand values to a branch without recording comparison semantics.
cards.prompt: Define Python comparison result. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A Python comparison result is produced by an equality, ordering, identity, or membership comparison.
Control flow truth-tests the comparison result when it uses that result as a condition.
The comparison result is not assumed to be either of the compared operands.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** An alternative falsifiable explanation for the same target symptom retained until evidence distinguishes it from the leading hypothesis rather than silently ignored after an intuition.

**Worked check.** For a stale total, compare 'wrong parser' against 'old file'. Log the file hash before parsing; a stale hash rejects the parser-only explanation.
major_error_concepts: Testing only the favored explanation and calling its survival unique causation.
cards.prompt: What does Python competing causal hypothesis diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A competing causal hypothesis is an alternative explanation for the same target symptom.
The alternative specifies its own causal mechanism and falsifiable prediction.
The alternative remains active until valid evidence distinguishes it from the leading hypothesis.
The investigation records why a probe favors, narrows, or rejects either explanation.
Intuition alone does not license silently discarding the competing explanation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A statement that controls one or more clauses and suites such as a conditional loop function definition or exception-handling construct.
major_error_concepts: Counting each clause header as an unrelated statement with no shared control relation.
cards.prompt: Define Python compound statement. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A statement that controls one or more clauses and suites such as a conditional loop function definition or exception-handling construct.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A truth-tested clause evaluated for each reached comprehension binding that skips the remaining inner work and result expression when false.
major_error_concepts: Applying the comprehension filter only after constructing every result element and executing rejected-item effects.
cards.prompt: Define Python comprehension filter. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A truth-tested clause evaluated for each reached comprehension binding that skips the remaining inner work and result expression when false.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A breakpoint whose pause request is gated by an evaluated condition allowing selection of a specific iteration or state while retaining condition errors and evaluation effects as risks.
major_error_concepts: Assuming condition evaluation cannot raise mutate state or alter timing.
cards.prompt: Define Python conditional breakpoint. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A conditional breakpoint requests a pause only when execution reaches its location and its condition is truthy.
The condition is evaluated in a specified debugger and frame context.
The condition can select a particular iteration or state among repeated reaches.
Condition-evaluation errors are part of the debugger evidence.
Condition evaluation may itself have side effects or timing costs.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The expression form selecting and evaluating exactly one of two value expressions according to a middle condition while producing a value for a larger expression.
major_error_concepts: Treating both alternative expressions as evaluated before the condition chooses a result.
cards.prompt: Define Python conditional expression. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A Python conditional expression uses a middle condition to select between two value expressions.
Exactly one of the two value expressions is evaluated.
The selected expression supplies the value of the conditional expression.
The value selected by a Python conditional expression can participate in a larger enclosing expression.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An `if` compound statement that evaluates clause conditions in source order and executes at most one selected suite before continuing after the construct.
major_error_concepts: Executing multiple true clause suites as though each clause were an independent `if`.
cards.prompt: Define Python conditional statement. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An `if` compound statement that evaluates clause conditions in source order and executes at most one selected suite before continuing after the construct.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An observable mutation input read output write or external action caused when an iterator is advanced rather than necessarily when its iterator object is constructed.
major_error_concepts: Scheduling effects at iterator construction without evidence of eager behavior.
cards.prompt: Define Python consumption side effect. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A consumption side effect is an observable action caused when an iterator is advanced.
A consumption side effect may be a mutation, input read, output write, or external action.
The side effect need not occur when the iterator object is constructed.
The trace must associate the effect with the particular advancement that caused it.

accepted_variants: It skips the remaining ordinary body statements and requests the nearest loop's next cycle: condition test for while, next item for for. It does not skip finally, which runs before that cycle and can change the transfer.
cards.definition: continue requests the next iteration of the nearest enclosing loop, skipping the remaining ordinary body path. A while loop retests its condition; a for loop requests its next item. Applicable finally/context-manager cleanup runs before that continuation, unless it replaces the transfer.
major_error_concepts: Treating continue as break or as a way to bypass required cleanup.
cards.prompt: Describe Python continue and explain whether it bypasses finally cleanup.
required_concepts: It targets the next cycle of the nearest loop rather than exiting that loop.
Applicable cleanup still runs before the next condition check or item request and may alter the pending transfer.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A wrong reachable path repetition count exit mode or skipped effect attributed to specific condition ordering truth semantics update placement or transfer behavior with a minimized counterexample.
major_error_concepts: Repairing final output directly without identifying the control decision that caused it.
cards.prompt: Define Python control-flow defect. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A Python control-flow defect produces a wrong reachable path, repetition count, exit mode, or skipped effect.
The defect is attributed to a specific condition order, truth rule, update placement, or control transfer.
The attribution is supported by a minimized counterexample.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** A probe run that changes only the declared observation or test condition while holding source input environment and target behavior fixed enough to interpret the difference.

**Worked check.** Insert `print(repr(value), type(value))` immediately before one branch, hold input fixed, and compare one run with the probe removed; the observation targets one hypothesis.
major_error_concepts: Changing code input and instrumentation together and assigning the outcome to one factor.
cards.prompt: What does Python controlled diagnostic probe diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A controlled diagnostic probe changes only the declared observation or test condition.
The probe holds source identity fixed unless source change is the declared condition.
The probe holds input and relevant initial state fixed.
The probe holds environment and target-behavior definition fixed enough for comparison.
The resulting difference is interpreted only within the controlled dimensions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A versioned source change limited to the declared repair mechanism with unrelated formatting refactoring input and environment held fixed enough for before-after attribution.
major_error_concepts: Combining repair refactor and input changes then crediting one mechanism.
cards.prompt: Define Python controlled repair edit. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A controlled repair edit is a versioned source change limited to the declared repair mechanism.
Unrelated formatting and refactoring remain fixed for the comparison.
Input and relevant initial state remain fixed.
Interpreter, environment, and observation procedure remain fixed enough for attribution.
The before-and-after source lineage and exact diff are retained.

accepted_variants: b=a aliases a. For a list, b=a.copy() gives a separate outer list but can share nested objects. Immutable operations such as tuple(existing_tuple) can return the original object, so copying is not a universal fresh-identity promise.
cards.definition: An alias is another reference to the same object. Copying a mutable built-in container such as a list produces a distinct outer container, but shallow copies can still share contained objects. Immutable copy/conversion operations may reuse an existing object, so identity conclusions must be tied to the specific operation and type.
major_error_concepts: Equating shallow copy with recursive independence.
Universalizing a new-object guarantee to immutable operations.
cards.prompt: Distinguish aliasing from copying, including nested sharing and whether immutable-copy operations guarantee a new identity.
required_concepts: Aliasing preserves object identity; a mutable built-in container copy such as list.copy gives a separate outer container.
A shallow container copy retains references to contained objects.
Do not require new object identity for every immutable copy/conversion operation.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** A field-by-field comparison between the specified target state and measured snapshot at a matched execution boundary with missing unobserved and representation-limited fields marked explicitly.

**Worked check.** Expected prefix sums are `[1,3,6]`; observed values are `[1,3,5]`. The first informative divergence is the third update, not the final print.
major_error_concepts: Comparing states from different iterations frames or source releases as though aligned.
cards.prompt: What does Python debugging expected-observed comparison diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: An expected-observed debug comparison aligns one specified target state with one measured snapshot at the same execution boundary.
The comparison evaluates corresponding fields individually.
Fields absent from the snapshot are marked missing rather than treated as matching.
Fields outside the observation procedure are marked unobserved.
Representation-limited fields are marked separately from measured equality or difference.
Each reported mismatch retains its expected and observed values.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** The source and execution boundary where a symptom or exception becomes observable which may be downstream from the earlier transition that created invalid state.

**Worked check.** `10 / d` raises on line 8 when `d=0`; line 8 is the failure site, while the defect may be the earlier parser that admitted zero.
major_error_concepts: Treating the reported source line as proof that the defect originated there.
cards.prompt: What does Python debugging failure site diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A debugging failure site is the source and execution boundary where a symptom or exception becomes observable.
The site is bound to one source artifact and reached control state.
The site may be downstream from the transition that first created invalid state.
The site supplies a starting observation point rather than proof of causation.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** The first observed execution boundary where a declared state predicate required for later reasoning is false with its prior holding state and transition evidence preserved.

**Worked check.** For a running sum, check `total == sum(items[:i])` after each iteration. The first false check identifies the transition that broke the invariant.
major_error_concepts: Inventing an invariant after failure solely to match the observed symptom.
cards.prompt: What does Python debugging invariant violation diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A debugging invariant violation occurs when a declared state predicate required for later reasoning is observed false.
The violation is bound to the first observed execution boundary at the selected trace grain.
Evidence retains the prior compared boundary where the predicate still held.
Evidence retains the transition between the holding and violating states.
An observed violation does not by itself prove which source defect caused the transition.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** A captured value control position frame effect or output from a recorded execution with tool point timing and possible observer influence recorded separately from interpretation.

**Worked check.** Record `i=2`, `value='3'`, `type=str`, and source line 14; 'the loop looks wrong' is not a reproducible observation.
major_error_concepts: Mixing inferred intent into the field labeled as directly observed state.
cards.prompt: What does Python debugging observation diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A debugging observation captures a value, control position, frame, effect, or output from one recorded execution.
The observation records the tool or probe point used for capture.
The observation records when capture occurred relative to the relevant transition.
Possible observer influence is recorded separately from the measured content.
Interpretation of the observation is kept distinct from the captured evidence.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** A temporary structured output statement placed to capture a hypothesis-relevant state boundary with probe identity expected value and potential behavior change documented.

**Worked check.** Print `repr(key)` just before dictionary lookup. Seeing `'id\n'` rather than `'id'` tests the whitespace hypothesis without claiming the print fixes it.
major_error_concepts: Leaving ad hoc prints scattered through code without mapping them to hypotheses.
cards.prompt: What does Python debug-print probe diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A debug-print probe is a temporary structured output statement at one selected state boundary.
The probe has an identity that can be matched to its emitted record.
The probe captures state relevant to a named causal hypothesis.
The expected value or distinguishing pattern is declared before the run.
Potential timing, formatting, or state effects from printing are documented.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A bounded record of selected bindings values identities control position stack and external observations at one probe point with capture method and mutability limitations explicit.
major_error_concepts: Calling a shallow displayed snapshot a complete frozen copy of program state.
cards.prompt: Define Python debugging state snapshot. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A debug-state snapshot is a bounded record captured at one identified probe point.
The snapshot records selected bindings, values, and object identities.
The snapshot records the control position and selected call-stack context.
The snapshot records selected external observations.
The snapshot records its capture method.
The snapshot states mutability, representation, and omitted-state limitations.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** The externally or internally observed mismatch exception hang or state anomaly that triggered investigation kept distinct from its execution location and underlying causal defect.

**Worked check.** A blank report is the observed symptom. It does not distinguish an empty query, a filtered dataframe, or a failed writer until evidence separates them.
major_error_concepts: Naming the first visible symptom as the proven root cause automatically.
cards.prompt: What does Python debugging symptom diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A debugging symptom is an observed mismatch, exception, hang, or state anomaly that triggered investigation.
The symptom is bound to a recorded execution and observation procedure.
The symptom is distinct from the source or execution location where it became visible.
The symptom is distinct from the underlying causal defect.
The symptom definition includes the exact condition that counts as recurrence.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** The specified expected output state transition failure disposition or external effect against which one observed small-program execution is compared during a bounded investigation.

**Worked check.** Freeze the target as `normalize(' A ') == 'a'` and no stdout. A vague goal such as 'clean strings' is insufficient to judge a repair.
major_error_concepts: Changing the intended behavior after seeing the implementation's current output.
cards.prompt: What does Python debugging target behavior diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A debugging target behavior specifies the expected output, state transition, failure disposition, or external effect.
The target is scoped to one bounded small-program execution and input state.
The target identifies the observation boundary at which comparison is valid.
Observed execution evidence is compared directly against the specified target.
A target behavior is an expectation rather than an observation of the failing run.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Examination of an upstream frame's arguments locals and next control location to determine whether invalid state was created or merely passed through that call boundary.
major_error_concepts: Restricting diagnosis to the innermost frame when the caller supplied invalid state.
cards.prompt: Define Python debugger caller inspection. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Debugger caller inspection selects an upstream suspended frame.
The inspection records that caller's arguments and local bindings.
The inspection records the caller's next control location.
The evidence tests whether invalid state was created before the call boundary.
The evidence distinguishes state creation in the caller from mere passage through that boundary.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A resume action that runs until another breakpoint stop event exception interruption or program termination rather than advancing exactly one source line or frame.
major_error_concepts: Using continue when the investigation requires observing every intermediate state transition.
cards.prompt: Define Python debugger `continue` command. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A debugger `continue` command resumes suspended execution without requesting the next single-step boundary.
Execution proceeds until a configured breakpoint or other debugger stop event.
An exception or explicit interruption can stop continued execution.
Program termination can end the continue action without another pause.
The command does not promise advancement by exactly one source line or one frame.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The debugger-selected execution frame whose source context and namespaces receive inspection commands while remaining distinct from the innermost traceback frame and the program's top frame.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every debugger expression uses locals from the failure's innermost frame.
cards.prompt: Define Python debugger current frame. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The debugger current frame is the selected suspended execution frame.
Inspection commands use that frame's source context and namespaces.
The current frame may be changed through stack-navigation commands.
The selected frame is distinct from the innermost traceback frame unless explicitly aligned.
The selected frame is distinct from the program's top-level frame unless explicitly selected.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Evaluation of an expression in the selected suspended context to inspect or compute state while retaining that calls properties iteration and assignments can change program behavior.
major_error_concepts: Treating arbitrary debugger evaluation as a passive read with no possible effects.
cards.prompt: Define Python debugger expression evaluation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Debugger expression evaluation runs one expression in the selected suspended context.
Name lookup and operations use that frame's current state.
Function calls or property access in the expression may cause side effects.
Iteration in the expression may consume lazy state.
Assignment-capable debugger commands may mutate objects or bindings.
The evaluated result is evidence from the altered or unaltered state actually produced by the command.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Observation of bindings and object representations in the selected frame at a pause with aliasing lazy evaluation and representation limits retained in the evidence record.
major_error_concepts: Reading displayed representations as complete deep immutable snapshots of all objects.
cards.prompt: Define Python debugger local-state inspection. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Local-state inspection observes selected bindings in the debugger's current frame at one pause.
The evidence records object representations and relevant identity relations.
Aliasing limits are preserved when multiple names may reach the same object.
Lazy values are not assumed fully evaluated merely because their references are visible.
Representation output is not assumed to expose all internal or external state.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The possibility that debugger commands or evaluated expressions mutate objects consume iterators advance external resources or otherwise make the inspected execution differ from the original failure.
major_error_concepts: Using post-mutation observations as though they came from the untouched failing run.
cards.prompt: Define Python debugger mutation risk. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Debugger mutation risk is the possibility that inspection commands change the suspended execution.
Evaluated calls or properties may mutate reachable objects.
Iterator inspection may consume values and advance producer state.
Debugger actions may advance external resources or alter timing.
A mutated debug run is distinguished from the original failure execution in the evidence record.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A resume action that advances execution to the next stoppable location in the current frame while called functions ordinarily run without interactive entry unless another stop intervenes.
major_error_concepts: Assuming next skips execution of the called function or every nested breakpoint.
cards.prompt: Define Python debugger `next` command. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A debugger `next` command resumes suspended execution.
The command seeks the next stoppable location in the current frame under debugger semantics.
Called functions ordinarily run without interactive entry during `next`.
A breakpoint or other stop event inside a call may intervene.
Return, exception, or termination can prevent reaching a later location in the original frame.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The suspended execution context at one debugger stop including selected frame next statement locals globals stack and pending control state before a resume command.
major_error_concepts: Confusing the highlighted next statement with one that has already executed.
cards.prompt: Define Python debugger pause state. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A debugger pause state is the suspended execution context at one recorded stop.
The state identifies the selected frame and next statement boundary.
The state records selected local and global bindings.
The state records the suspended call stack.
The state records any pending return, exception, or other control outcome visible to the debugger.
The pause state precedes the next resume command.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** A specified interactive debugging execution with source input debugger configuration breakpoints commands observations and termination outcome preserved sufficiently to reconstruct its diagnostic path.

**Worked check.** Break at `parse`, run `p raw`, `next`, and `p result`, and record source hash plus commands; the resulting path can be reconstructed without treating it as a rerun proof.
major_error_concepts: Citing an unreproducible interactive impression with no source or command receipt.
cards.prompt: What does Python debugger session diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A debugger session is one specified interactive debugging execution.
The session binds exact source, input, environment, and debugger configuration.
The session records configured breakpoints and issued commands in order.
The session records observations at each relevant stop.
The session records its termination outcome.
The preserved record is sufficient to reconstruct the diagnostic path within declared limits.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Selection among suspended caller and callee frames to inspect their distinct code contexts and bindings without changing which runtime frame originally raised or paused.
major_error_concepts: Treating debugger frame selection as a runtime return or call-stack mutation.
cards.prompt: Define Python debugger stack navigation. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Debugger stack navigation selects among suspended caller and callee frames.
Each selected frame has its own source context and name bindings.
Navigation changes the frame used by inspection commands.
Navigation does not change which runtime frame originally raised the exception or triggered the pause.
Navigation alone does not resume or mutate program control flow.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A resume action that advances to the next stoppable execution location while entering called functions according to debugger semantics and updating the selected frame context.
major_error_concepts: Expecting step to remain within the current frame like next.
cards.prompt: Define Python debugger `step` command. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A debugger `step` command resumes suspended execution.
The command advances to the next stoppable execution location under debugger semantics.
The command enters called functions when their execution provides a stoppable location.
The selected frame context can change after the step.
Breakpoints, exceptions, or termination may stop execution before the anticipated location.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Repeated binding of the same stored default object on calls that omit an optional argument rather than construction of an equal fresh object each time.
major_error_concepts: Drawing a new default object for every call without a body-level constructor.
cards.prompt: Define Python default-object reuse. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Repeated binding of the same stored default object on calls that omit an optional argument rather than construction of an equal fresh object each time.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An expression evaluated when the function definition executes whose resulting object is stored for later calls that omit the corresponding optional parameter.
major_error_concepts: Re-evaluating every stored default expression automatically during each later function invocation event.
cards.prompt: Define Python default-parameter expression. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An expression evaluated when the function definition executes whose resulting object is stored for later calls that omit the corresponding optional parameter.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An explicit runtime predicate at a trust or contract boundary that rejects unsupported state through a documented ordinary or exceptional interface before unsafe downstream use.
major_error_concepts: Adding redundant checks everywhere without defining ownership or failure disposition.
cards.prompt: Define Python defensive check. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A defensive check evaluates an explicit runtime predicate at a declared trust or contract boundary.
The predicate identifies unsupported input or program state before unsafe downstream use.
Failure produces a documented ordinary or exceptional interface.
The check remains active in every supported execution configuration.
The check is scoped to the invariant that the downstream operation actually requires.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** The ordered suite stored for execution only after a successful call creates a callee frame and binds parameters rather than when its `def` statement executes.

**Worked check.** `def f(): return missing` defines successfully; `f()` later raises `NameError`. Compilation of the body does not resolve that global name.
major_error_concepts: Recording function-body effects at definition time merely because the source is visible.
cards.prompt: What boundary or limitation does Python deferred function body impose?
required_concepts: The ordered suite stored for execution only after a successful call creates a callee frame and binds parameters rather than when its `def` statement executes.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The reached runtime event that evaluates definition-time expressions creates the function object and performs its name binding while deferring ordinary body statements until calls.
major_error_concepts: Evaluating every default and body expression anew as part of source parsing.
cards.prompt: Define Python definition-execution event. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A Python definition-execution event occurs when runtime control reaches a function definition.
The event evaluates the definition-time expressions.
The event creates the function object and performs its name binding.
The event defers ordinary function-body statements until a later call.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The specific trace value branch frame effect or outcome expected if a causal hypothesis is true at a declared observation point and input condition.
major_error_concepts: Choosing or revising the predicted value after observing the probe result from the recorded run.
cards.prompt: Define Python diagnostic prediction. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The specific trace value branch frame effect or outcome expected if a causal hypothesis is true at a declared observation point and input condition.

cards.definition:
**Definition.** A deliberately placed observation or bounded intervention selected to distinguish causal hypotheses through a predeclared prediction while minimizing unrelated state and timing changes.

**Worked check.** For a suspected text/integer mismatch, capture `repr(x)` and `type(x)` at the comparison; `'2'` and `2` become distinguishable evidence.
major_error_concepts: Adding many untracked prints until output looks informative without a hypothesis.
cards.prompt: What does Python diagnostic probe diagnose or distinguish?
required_concepts: A diagnostic probe is a deliberately placed observation or bounded intervention.
The probe is selected to distinguish named causal hypotheses.
Each hypothesis has a predeclared prediction for the probe result.
The probe minimizes unrelated state and timing changes.
The probe records its identity, placement, and measured outcome.

cards.definition: **Definition.** In-place creation or replacement of one key association after key and value evaluation with dictionary identity preserved and existing-key position behavior kept explicit.
major_error_concepts: Assuming every dictionary assignment appends a duplicate key-value item even when an equal key already exists.
cards.prompt: Define Python dictionary assignment. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Dictionary assignment evaluates the key and value expressions before applying the association.
Assignment creates a key association when no equal key is present.
Assignment replaces the associated value when an equal key is already present.
Dictionary assignment mutates the existing dictionary while preserving its identity.
The contract records how replacing an existing key affects its insertion position.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A comprehension that evaluates one key and value expression for each surviving binding combination and builds a new dictionary with later equal keys overwriting prior values.
major_error_concepts: Assuming duplicate equal generated keys create multiple dictionary items instead of later values overwriting earlier associations.
cards.prompt: Define Python dictionary comprehension. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A dictionary comprehension iterates through its declared binding clauses and optional filters.
For each surviving binding combination, it evaluates one key expression and one value expression.
The comprehension constructs a new dictionary.
When later produced keys compare equal to earlier keys, the later value overwrites the prior value for that key.

cards.definition: **Definition.** In-place removal of the association for a requested key through deletion or pop semantics with absent-key behavior and optional returned value distinguished.
major_error_concepts: Deleting the value object itself or shifting numeric indexes afterward.
cards.prompt: Define Python dictionary deletion. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: In-place removal of the association for a requested key through deletion or pop semantics with absent-key behavior and optional returned value distinguished.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A nonmutating lookup returning the associated value when present or a supplied default or `None` when absent without distinguishing absence from an equal stored default by result alone.
major_error_concepts: Treating `get` as insertion of the fallback value into the dictionary.
cards.prompt: Define Python dictionary `get`. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Dictionary `get` performs a nonmutating key lookup.
When the key is present, `get` returns its associated value.
When the key is absent, `get` returns the supplied default or implicit `None`.
The result alone cannot distinguish an absent key from a present key storing a value equal to the chosen default.

accepted_variants: With d={'a':1}, item=next(iter(d.items())) gives ('a',1). After d['a']=2, item remains ('a',1), while list(d.items()) contains ('a',2). The view is dynamic; an already-yielded tuple is not rewritten, although a mutable value it references can itself change.
cards.definition: A dictionary item is a key-value association. dict.items() provides a dynamic view, but iterating that view yields a (key, value) tuple holding the references obtained for that item. Rebinding the dictionary's value later does not rewrite an already-yielded tuple; a mutable object referenced by the tuple may still change.
major_error_concepts: Confusing a dynamic view with a live-updating yielded tuple.
Calling the yielded pair a deep copy of its contents.
cards.prompt: Distinguish the dynamic dict.items() view from a (key, value) tuple already yielded by iterating it.
required_concepts: The items view reflects the dictionary's current entries.
An already-yielded item tuple is not rewritten by later dictionary rebinding, although its referenced mutable objects may change.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The insertion order preserved by current dictionary iteration after updates and deletions while remaining distinct from sorted key order and semantic record priority.
major_error_concepts: Reporting lexicographic sorting or arbitrary order as the documented dictionary rule.
cards.prompt: Define Python dictionary iteration order. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Current Python dictionary iteration preserves insertion order.
Updating an existing association follows the dictionary's documented position behavior.
Deleting and later reinserting a key can affect its iteration position.
Dictionary iteration order is distinct from sorted key order.
Dictionary iteration order does not by itself encode semantic record priority.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The ordinary `in` test over dictionary keys rather than values or items producing a truth result without retrieving the mapped value.
major_error_concepts: Treating `value in mapping` as ordinary search through mapped values.
cards.prompt: Define Python dictionary-key membership. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The ordinary `in` test over dictionary keys rather than values or items producing a truth result without retrieving the mapped value.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A hashable object used under equality and hash consistency to identify at most one association in a dictionary while remaining distinct from its mapped value.
major_error_concepts: Assuming keys are always strings or compared only by identity.
cards.prompt: Define Python dictionary key. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A hashable object used under equality and hash consistency to identify at most one association in a dictionary while remaining distinct from its mapped value.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Retrieval of the value associated with an equal hash-compatible key using subscription syntax or a key error when no association exists.
major_error_concepts: Searching mapped values or numerical insertion positions when Python evaluates a dictionary key-subscription operation.
cards.prompt: Define Python dictionary lookup. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Retrieval of the value associated with an equal hash-compatible key using subscription syntax or a key error when no association exists.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A mutable insertion-ordered mapping from unique hashable keys to object references with lookup update deletion membership and iteration defined by key identity and equality rules.
major_error_concepts: Treating a dictionary as an unordered list of two-element records with numeric positions.
cards.prompt: Define Python dictionary object. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A Python dictionary is a mutable insertion-ordered mapping.
Dictionary keys are unique under the mapping's equality and hash rules.
Dictionary keys must satisfy the hashability protocol.
Each current key is associated with an object reference.
Dictionaries support lookup, update, deletion, membership, and iteration.
Key identity, equality, and hashing jointly govern association behavior.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Any object reference associated with a dictionary key which need not be unique hashable immutable or searched by ordinary key membership.
major_error_concepts: Applying dictionary key hashability uniqueness and immutability restrictions automatically to every associated mapped value object.
cards.prompt: Define Python dictionary value. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Any object reference associated with a dictionary key which need not be unique hashable immutable or searched by ordinary key membership.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A call-time type error caused when one parameter would receive more than one value through overlapping positional keyword or unpacked argument sources.
major_error_concepts: Silently selecting the later argument value and discarding the earlier binding source.
cards.prompt: Define Python duplicate-argument-binding failure. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A call-time type error caused when one parameter would receive more than one value through overlapping positional keyword or unpacked argument sources.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A return transfer reached before the syntactic body end to terminate a specific path after sufficient result or failure information is available.
major_error_concepts: Assuming later cleanup or state updates execute after an early return without `finally` semantics.
cards.prompt: Define Python early return. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A return transfer reached before the syntactic body end to terminate a specific path after sufficient result or failure information is available.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A later condition-and-suite pair evaluated only when all preceding clauses in the same conditional statement failed to select a suite.
major_error_concepts: Evaluating every `elif` condition for logging even after a branch was selected.
cards.prompt: Define Python `elif` clause. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A later condition-and-suite pair evaluated only when all preceding clauses in the same conditional statement failed to select a suite.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The optional unconditional fallback suite selected only when every preceding `if` and `elif` condition in the same statement tests false.
major_error_concepts: Treating `else` as a separate condition that can also fail or run after success.
cards.prompt: Define Python conditional `else` clause. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The optional unconditional fallback suite selected only when every preceding `if` and `elif` condition in the same statement tests false.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A lexically surrounding function scope consulted for free-name lookup by a nested function when no local binding shadows that name.
major_error_concepts: Looking only in local and global namespaces for every function name lookup.
cards.prompt: Define Python enclosing-function scope. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A lexically surrounding function scope consulted for free-name lookup by a nested function when no local binding shadows that name.

cards.definition: **Definition.** An encode or decode exception produced when input cannot be represented or interpreted under the selected codec and strictness policy with failure position retained.
major_error_concepts: Replacing invalid data silently and then claiming an exact round trip.
cards.prompt: Define Python encoding-conversion failure. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: An encoding-conversion failure occurs when selected text or bytes cannot be represented or interpreted by the chosen codec.
The strictness or error policy participates in whether conversion raises an exception.
The failure records whether the operation was encoding or decoding.
The failure evidence retains the position and offending input region when available.
An encoding failure is distinct from later application-schema validation.

cards.definition: **Definition.** Lazy pairing of each consumed iterable item with a counter beginning at a declared start while preserving item order and iterator exhaustion.
major_error_concepts: Using the enumeration counter as proof of a source container index.
cards.prompt: Define Python `enumerate` iteration. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: Lazy pairing of each consumed iterable item with a counter beginning at a declared start while preserving item order and iterator exhaustion.

cards.definition: **Definition.** One evidence-bearing runtime step in which a reached expression or statement consumes a prior state and yields a value state transition control transfer side effect or exception.
major_error_concepts: Collapsing a compound expression into one result and losing intermediate effects or failures.
cards.prompt: Define Python evaluation event. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A Python evaluation event occurs when execution reaches one expression or statement.
The event consumes a prior execution state.
The event may yield a value or a state transition.
The event may yield a control transfer or observable side effect.
The event may instead yield an exception.
The event is retained as evidence for explaining the execution trace.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The ordered sequence of evaluation events required by the bound syntax and runtime context including skipped branches short circuits calls and exceptions.
major_error_concepts: Reordering subexpressions because ordinary arithmetic would produce the same pure value.
cards.prompt: Define Python evaluation-order trace. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: The ordered sequence of evaluation events required by the bound syntax and runtime context including skipped branches short circuits calls and exceptions.

cards.definition: **Definition.** A handler clause declaring one accepted exception class relation optional object binding and suite that becomes eligible only for matching exceptions from its associated try execution.
major_error_concepts: Treating an except clause as a conditional that examines ordinary return values.
cards.prompt: Define Python `except` clause. Include its essential conditions and distinctions.
required_concepts: A Python `except` clause declares an accepted exception class relation.
The clause may bind the matched exception object to a target name.
The clause becomes eligible only for matching exceptions from its associated `try` execution.
Clause ordering participates when more than one handler could match.
The selected clause executes its own handler suite.

cards.definition: **Definition.** The recorded relation between an exception raised while another exception is active and its prior context allowing higher-level failure meaning and lower-level evidence to remain distinguishable.
major_error_concepts: Replacing a low-level exception and discarding every link to its original evidence.

cards.definition:
In an ordinary function, assigning to a name anywhere in the body ordinarily makes it local unless declared global or nonlocal. Reading it before its local value is bound raises UnboundLocalError rather than using an outer value.

```python
x = 1
def f():
    print(x)
    x = 2
```
